newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds rise amid political uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds rise amid political uncertainty.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Wednesday as investors returned to the bond market amid growing political uncertainty, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.02 pct to 104.18
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.06 to 103.36
Volume was a moderate 122 million shekels.

"The peace process is stuck and political uncertainty is growing. Investors prefer bonds over stocks because nobody wants to take any risks now," said Gidi Halperin of Meitav Investments and Securities.

U.S. President Bill Clinton has ordered his Middle East peace envoy back to the region to try and salvage Israeli-PLO talks threatened by recent unrest. Ross was due to meet Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat in Morocco on Thursday.

"With so much uncertainty, inflation-linked bonds are the safest investment tool. Investors also fear that the rise of the dollar and the closure of the West Bank may lead to rising inflation," said Michael Weiss of Evergreen Capital Markets.
Israel sealed off the Palestinian West Bank and Gaza on Friday after a Hamas Islamic militant killed himself and three Israeli women in a suicide bombing in Tel Aviv.
Unlinked bonds closed higher. "These bonds offer yields of 14.8 percent, which is still attractive," Halperin said. "The Makams also rose because private investors prefer them for tax reasons."

Dollar-linked bonds ended lower despite the rise of the dollar against the shekel, but traders said they are expected to rise on Thursday. In the local forex market the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3700 shekels against 3.3660 on Tuesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
